caption: Figure 1. Overview of BLIP-2's framework. We pre-train a lightweight Querying Transformer following a two-stage strategy to bridge the modality gap. The first stage bootstraps visionlanguage representation learning from a frozen image encoder. The second stage bootstraps vision-to-language generative learning from a frozen LLM, which enables zero-shot instructed image-totext generation (see Figure 4 for more examples).

This figure is a diagram showing two methods of bootstrapping vision-to-language generative pre-training using large language models (LLMs). The top panel demonstrates bootstrapping from a decoder-based LLM (e.g., OPT), while the bottom panel shows bootstrapping from an encoder-decoder-based LLM (e.g., FlanT5). Both methods involve an image encoder, a Q-Former, and a fully-connected layer that adapts the output dimension of the Q-Former to the input dimension of the chosen LLM.

description:
## Figure Description
This figure illustrates the model architecture for Visual Question Answering (VQA) finetuning. It shows the process flow from an input image to the final answer. The image is encoded into features, which are then processed by a Q-Former to generate relevant image features. These features, along with the question, are input into a Large Language Model (LLM) to predict the answer.
